§6Coker Naphtha§f

§aMedium-grade coker byproduct - reform it for reformate gas or mix it into solvent!§f

Coker Naphtha is a flammable, combustible, polluting viscous liquid with a medium fuel grade at §e125 kTU§f and §e187 kHE§f per bucket. It is a common byproduct when coking lighter fluids in the §bCoker Unit§f.

§6Production§f (Coker Unit):
§b•§f Cracked Naphtha (§e6,400mB§f) → §e640mB§f Coker Naphtha.
§b•§f Reclaimed Industrial Oil (§e5,800mB§f) → §e580mB§f.
§b•§f Naphtha (§e4,900mB§f) → §e490mB§f.
§b•§f Diesel (§e590mB§f) → §e59mB§f.

§6Uses§f:
§b•§f Catalytic Reformer: §e1,000mB§f → §e500mB§f Reformate + §e100mB§f Reformate Gas + §e50mB§f Liquid Hydrogen.
§b•§f Fractioning Tower: §e100mB§f → §e75mB§f Cracked Naphtha + §e25mB§f Cracked Light Oil.
§b•§f Industrial Mixer: §e500mB§f + §e500mB§f Aromatic Hydrocarbons → §e1,000mB§f Solvent.

§ePS:§f Coker Naphtha is decent fuel but much more valuable when reformed. The §bCatalytic Reformer§f route gives Reformate Gas - the §e100mB§f per §e1,000mB§f adds up fast with large coker batches!
